pr.title: CI: run the regression tests on MySQL
pr.body:
## Summary

CI now also runs the full regression suite on MySQL, alongside the internal database and PostgreSQL. The MySQL and PostgreSQL connections write command parameters into the SQL themselves rather than binding them, so each needs its own run.

## Changes

- **`tests.yml`:** the `database` input also accepts `mysql`. The new step "Move the server to MySQL" uses the runner image's MySQL 8.0:
  - creates a data directory with `--initialize-insecure`, using an options file of its own (`--defaults-file`) so none of the image's option files apply;
  - installs and starts mysqld as a Windows service on port 3307;
  - runs `CreateExternalDatabase`, `SetDefaultDatabase` and `Reinitialize`, as DBSetup does.
- **`build.yml`:** new `test-mysql` job, "Tests (MySQL)".
- **`TestFixtureBase.TearDown`:** a failed test now prints its failure message and the errors the server logged, as it happens. The console runner only prints failures at the end of a run, and a run that hits the job timeout never gets there.

## What the first runs found

1. **MySQL stopped after the setup step.** The runner ends every process a step started when the step ends, so a mysqld started with `Start-Process` was gone before the tests began. Every test then failed in setup, after about 76 seconds of `Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (10061)`, and the job hit its 120-minute timeout. mysqld now runs as a service, as PostgreSQL does. The cause only became visible through the TearDown output above.
2. **Writes were slow.** By default MySQL 8 waits for two disk flushes on every autocommit write. The options file therefore turns the binary log off and sets `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2`. On the Hyper-V test VM, a setting write went from 200 ms to 4.5 ms, and `API.UtilitiesTests` from 267 s to 26 s (17 s on the internal database). The database is thrown away with the runner, so durability doesn't matter.

## Verification

All three test jobs give the same result as the baseline:

| Run | Total | Passed | Failed | Inconclusive | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tests (MySQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (PostgreSQL) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |
| Tests (internal) | 1,294 | 1,185 | 0 | 34 | 75 |

This gives a MySQL baseline for 1.1c (MySQL prepared statements). The publish job still depends only on the build and the internal-database tests.

files.patch:
@@ -757,6 +757,17 @@ jobs:
       runner-image: ${{ needs.build.outputs.runner-image }}
       database: postgresql
 
+  # And against the MySQL server of the runner image, for the same reason, and like the
+  # PostgreSQL run not yet one the publish job waits for.
+  test-mysql:
+    name: Tests (MySQL)
+    needs: build
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/tests.yml
+    with:
+      installer-artifact: installer-untested
+      runner-image: ${{ needs.build.outputs.runner-image }}
+      database: mysql
+
   publish:
     name: Publish the installer
     needs: [build, test]

@@ -31,7 +31,8 @@ on:
         default: Debug
       database:
         description: 'Database the installed server runs on: internal (SQL Server Compact, what
-          a silent install sets up) or postgresql (the PostgreSQL server of the runner image).
+          a silent install sets up), postgresql (the PostgreSQL server of the runner image) or
+          mysql (the MySQL server of the runner image, on a data directory of its own).
           The MySQL and PostgreSQL connections write their command parameters into the SQL
           themselves rather than binding them, so they need runs of their own.'
         required: false
@@ -70,7 +71,7 @@ jobs:
         run: |
           # A workflow_call input is whatever the caller passes; an unknown database would
           # otherwise quietly run the tests on the internal one.
-          if ($env:DATABASE -notin @('internal', 'postgresql')) { throw "The database must be internal or postgresql, was '$env:DATABASE'." }
+          if ($env:DATABASE -notin @('internal', 'postgresql', 'mysql')) { throw "The database must be internal, postgresql or mysql, was '$env:DATABASE'." }
 
           $setup = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'installer\*.exe') | Select-Object -First 1
           if (-not $setup) { throw "The '$env:INSTALLER_ARTIFACT' artifact contains no executable." }
@@ -132,6 +133,76 @@ jobs:
           if ($database.DatabaseType -ne $hDBTypePostgreSQL) { throw "The server runs on database type $($database.DatabaseType), not PostgreSQL." }
           "hMailServer now runs on PostgreSQL ($($database.ServerName), database $($database.DatabaseName), version $($database.CurrentVersion))"
 
+      - name: Move the server to MySQL
+        if: inputs.database == 'mysql'
+        run: |
+          # The runner image carries a MySQL server, but no data directory to run it on. A new
+          # one, initialised without a root password, is what a run needs - whatever service or
+          # password the image may come with.
+          $mysqld = Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files\MySQL' -Recurse -Filter 'mysqld.exe' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
+              Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
+          if (-not $mysqld) { throw "The runner image has no MySQL server." }
+          & $mysqld.FullName --version
+
+          # The server reads only this file (--defaults-file), not whatever option file the image
+          # put where mysqld looks by default.
+          #
+          # Its own port, clear of any instance the image starts. The default authentication,
+          # caching_sha2_password, is left as it is: libmariadb carries the plugin.
+          #
+          # Without the binary log, and with the redo log flushed once a second rather than at
+          # every commit: the server writes with autocommit, so by default each write waits for
+          # two disk flushes. On the test VM a setting write took 200 ms by default and 4.5 ms
+          # like this, and API.UtilitiesTests went from 267 seconds to 26 (17 on the internal
+          # database). Durability is no concern for a database thrown away with the runner.
+          $port = 3307
+          $dataDirectory = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'mysql-data'
+          $optionFile = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'mysql.ini'
+          @(
+              '[mysqld]'
+              "datadir=$($dataDirectory -replace '\\', '/')"
+              "port=$port"
+              'skip-log-bin'
+              'innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2'
+          ) | Set-Content -Path $optionFile -Encoding ascii
+
+          & $mysqld.FullName "--defaults-file=$optionFile" --initialize-insecure --console
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "mysqld --initialize-insecure failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
+
+          # A service, as the PostgreSQL server is. The runner ends every process a step started
+          # when the step ends, so a mysqld started here with Start-Process was gone by the time
+          # the tests ran: each test then failed in its setup after the server's connection
+          # attempts ("Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (10061)") had all timed out.
+          & $mysqld.FullName --install ArzoieTestMySQL "--defaults-file=$optionFile"
+          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "mysqld --install failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
+          Start-Service ArzoieTestMySQL
+
+          $deadline = (Get-Date).AddMinutes(2)
+          while (-not (Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1 -Port $port -InformationLevel Quiet -WarningAction SilentlyContinue)) {
+              if ((Get-Date) -gt $deadline) { Get-Content (Join-Path $dataDirectory '*.err'); throw "MySQL did not start listening on port $port." }
+              Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
+          }
+          "MySQL listens on port $port"
+
+          # The settings that decide how the server's writes behave, for the record.
+          $mysql = Join-Path (Split-Path $mysqld.FullName) 'mysql.exe'
+          & $mysql --no-defaults --host=127.0.0.1 "--port=$port" --user=root --table `
+              -e 'SELECT @@version, @@autocommit, @@transaction_isolation, @@innodb_lock_wait_timeout, @@sql_mode, @@lower_case_table_names, @@character_set_server'
+
+          # What DBSetup does: create the database and its tables, point hMailServer.ini at
+          # it, and have the server reconnect.
+          $application = New-Object -ComObject 'hMailServer.Application'
+          if (-not $application.Authenticate('Administrator', '')) { throw "Could not authenticate with the blank administrator password." }
+
+          $hDBTypeMySQL = 1
+          $application.Database.CreateExternalDatabase($hDBTypeMySQL, '127.0.0.1', $port, 'hmailserver', 'root', '')
+          $application.Database.SetDefaultDatabase($hDBTypeMySQL, '127.0.0.1', $port, 'hmailserver', 'root', '')
+          $application.Reinitialize()
+
+          $database = $application.Database
+          if ($database.DatabaseType -ne $hDBTypeMySQL) { throw "The server runs on database type $($database.DatabaseType), not MySQL." }
+          "hMailServer now runs on MySQL ($($database.ServerName), database $($database.DatabaseName), version $($database.CurrentVersion))"
+
       - name: Build the test solution
         env:
           CONFIGURATION: ${{ inputs.configuration }}

commit.message:
Run the regression tests on MySQL as well

Like PostgreSQL, the MySQL connection writes its command parameters into the
SQL, which only a run on MySQL exercises - including the single-pass
substitution of #9, which so far was only tested in the server's class tests.

With database: mysql, tests.yml initialises a data directory of its own for the
MySQL server of the runner image (mysqld --initialize-insecure, so root has no
password), starts it on port 3307, clear of anything the image runs, and moves
the server to it through the COM API as the PostgreSQL run does. The default
authentication, caching_sha2_password, is left as it is; libmariadb has the
plugin compiled in.

build.yml runs it as Tests (MySQL). The publish job does not wait for it yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CI: run the MySQL server without the binary log and per-commit flushes

The first MySQL run timed out after 120 minutes: every test took about 76
seconds and failed in its setup. The server writes with autocommit, and MySQL
8.0 by default flushes both the binary log and the InnoDB redo log at every
commit, so each write waits for two disk flushes.

On the Hyper-V test VM with the same MySQL 8.0.46, a setting write took 200 ms
by default and 4.5 ms with --skip-log-bin and
--innodb-flush-log-at-trx-commit=2. RegressionTests.API.UtilitiesTests went from
267 seconds to 26 (17 on the internal database), and
AntiSpam.AuthenticationResults from 63 to 7. Durability does not matter for a
database that is thrown away with the runner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Regression tests: print why a test failed when it fails

The console runner prints the failures only once the whole run is over. The
MySQL run ran into the job's timeout with every test failing, so it never got
there and the log said only which tests ran - not why they failed. TearDown now
prints the failure message and stack trace beside the server log it already
prints for a failed test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CI: run MySQL with --no-defaults, and print what the server logs on a failure

The MySQL run still failed every test, now with the reason: SetUp's
Domain.Save() threw "Failed to save object" after about 76 seconds each time,
while the same MySQL 8.0.46 passes those tests on the test VM. The 76 seconds
fit the 50-second innodb_lock_wait_timeout plus the rest of the setup.

- mysqld runs with --no-defaults, so no option file of the image's can change
  how it behaves; any it finds is printed, and so are the settings that decide
  how the writes of the server behave.
- TearDown prints the errors the server logged during a test, as it does the
  failure itself, rather than only putting them in a failure that is reported
  at the end of the run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CI: run the MySQL server as a service

The errors the server logged gave the cause: "Can't connect to server on
'127.0.0.1' (10061)". The runner ends every process a step started when that
step ends, so the mysqld started with Start-Process in the setup step was gone
before the tests began, and each test failed in its setup once the server's
connection attempts had timed out - about 76 seconds a test.

mysqld is installed as a service now, as the PostgreSQL server of the image is,
with an option file of its own (--defaults-file) rather than command line
options and --no-defaults. On the test VM the service started, and from a new
session it still answered, with log_bin 0, innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit 2 and
port 3307.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge master into techdebt/ci-mysql

Brings in #12, #14 and #15.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
